result.title: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
result.summary: Visual brain decoding translates neural activity into human-interpretable images. While recent EEG-to-image reconstruction methods rely on aligning EEG signals with pretrained visual embeddings to condition an image generator, we empirically demonstrate that stronger cross-modal alignment do not translate into comparable gains in reconstruction quality. This indicates that improving the input condition alone is insufficient; the generative process itself requires explicit supervision. Although Representation Alignment (REPA) offers a solution by guiding diffusion transformers with pretrained vision encoder features, we find that EEG-conditioned generators struggle to follow these fixed targets. To address this mismatch, we introduce generation-derived supervision (GDS): an image-conditioned teacher that translates static image-encoder features into the internal representation space of a diffusion transformer. Our EEG-conditioned student generator closely tracks these dynamic targets during denoising, discarding the teacher at inference. Evaluated on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG, our approach consistently outperforms conditioning-centric baselines, achieving state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 EEG 到图像重建，实证发现增强跨模态对齐并不能带来同等重建增益，于是提出生成派生监督：用图像条件教师把静态图像编码器特征翻译为扩散 Transformer 的内部表示空间，在去噪过程中为学生生成器提供动态目标，推理时丢弃教师。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心线索是「仅改进输入条件不足、需直接监督生成过程中的内部状态」，可能可供核查 latent 推理状态的轨迹级监督与贡献分配问题，但任务为图像生成，与 VLM 推理的可迁移性尚待判断。
